items.title: Ted Piltzecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 10, 2019
items.q: my mother is from New Orleans, she used to play some Al Hirt songs when I was younger and that was — I used to listen to that

ctx.x: Did you have an aha moment as a kid, like with music, that this could be something that I really want to pursue? Something that occurred, a recording or seeing somebody?

I think it would be nice to say yes and like many artists can say, “When I was in fourth grade somebody came through town and I was knocked out and never forgot it.” I don’t think I ever had one of those. And I’m a little maybe different from a lot of other great — not great but other artists, that I just sort of did it and it was something I did pretty well and I — okay, well I guess I’ll go to music school and I just meandered into music school and then I sort of got into it. I mean I didn’t really have a…

was a really formative time I think artistically and aesthetically. Before that I played in a drum corps and that basically was functioning to get me off the streets and keep me out of trouble, which it did. I’m very thankful for that. Some of the guys that were hanging around at the time got into trouble. So my mom said get away from this gang, join the drum corps. There were no more drums left so they gave me a bugle and I played the bugle and then I got to high school and I played the trumpet, seemed to be the…
